def: A lymphocyte of the innate immune system that kills virus-infected and tumor cells without prior sensitization, using perforin and granzymes. It is inhibited by normal MHC I on healthy cells.
A procedure combining endoscopy and x-ray contrast to image and treat the bile and pancreatic ducts. It can remove stones but may cause pancreatitis.
An infection spread by sexual contact, such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HPV and HIV.
The ring of smooth muscle at the esophagogastric junction that relaxes with swallowing and otherwise prevents reflux of stomach contents.
Sampling cells from a mass with a thin needle for cytologic evaluation, commonly used for thyroid nodules and lymph nodes.

A granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis of older adults affecting the temporal artery, causing headache, jaw claudication and risk of blindness. It is linked to polymyalgia rheumatica and treated with steroids.
A small-vessel vasculitis with necrotizing granulomas of the upper airways and lungs plus glomerulonephritis. It is associated with c-ANCA (PR3).
A syndrome of rapid kidney function loss over days to weeks with crescents on biopsy. Causes include anti-GBM disease, immune complex disease and ANCA vasculitis.
The large vein that returns blood from the head, neck, arms and upper chest to the right atrium.
A prostanoid made by platelets from arachidonic acid via cyclooxygenase. It promotes platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction, and is blocked by aspirin.
Injury and death of kidney tubular cells from ischemia or toxins, the most common cause of acute kidney injury in hospitalized patients. Muddy brown casts are seen in urine.
A psychiatric disorder of intrusive unwanted thoughts (obsessions) and repetitive behaviors (compulsions) performed to relieve anxiety. It is treated with SSRIs and exposure therapy.
An inherited phagocyte disorder with defective NADPH oxidase, so cells cannot make the respiratory burst. It causes recurrent infections by catalase-positive organisms, such as Staphylococcus aureus.
An HIV drug class (such as zidovudine, tenofovir, lamivudine) that mimics DNA building blocks and terminates viral DNA synthesis by reverse transcriptase.
A hormone released by ventricular myocytes in response to stretch. It promotes sodium excretion and vasodilation, and is elevated in heart failure.
A liver-made acute-phase protein that rises with inflammation or infection, used as a nonspecific marker.
A small-vessel vasculitis in people with asthma, with eosinophilia and granulomas, associated with p-ANCA. Also called Churg-Strauss syndrome.
The proportion of oxygen in the air a patient breathes, 0.21 in room air. It is raised with supplemental oxygen.
Injection of drugs into veins, a risk factor for endocarditis (especially of the tricuspid valve), HIV and hepatitis B and C.
A malignancy of myeloid precursors, marked by myeloblasts with Auer rods. It presents with anemia, infection and bleeding in adults.
The abnormal hemoglobin of sickle cell disease, caused by a glutamic acid to valine substitution in the beta chain. It polymerizes when deoxygenated, sickling red cells.

term: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders
def: The American Psychiatric Association's reference text defining criteria for psychiatric diagnoses.
A precancerous cervical lesion (moderate to severe dysplasia) from HPV, likely to progress to carcinoma if untreated.
A hypothalamic tripeptide that stimulates TSH and prolactin release from the anterior pituitary.
The main plasma protein carrying thyroid hormones. Only the free fraction is active; TBG changes alter total, not free, hormone levels.
The most common non-Hodgkin lymphoma, an aggressive tumor of large B cells in adults. It may arise at nodal or extranodal sites such as the testis.
Dilation of the abdominal aorta to at least 1.5 times normal diameter, linked to atherosclerosis, smoking and hypertension. Rupture causes severe pain and shock; screening uses ultrasound.
A receptor tyrosine kinase gene. Rearrangements (EML4-ALK) occur in some lung adenocarcinomas, which respond to crizotinib.
The enzyme that breaks down acetylcholine at synapses. In amniotic fluid, high levels with alpha-fetoprotein suggest a neural tube defect.
The largest branch of the internal carotid, supplying the lateral cerebral cortex. Occlusion causes contralateral face and arm weakness and aphasia or neglect.
A ligand-gated chloride channel that mediates fast inhibition in the brain. Benzodiazepines, barbiturates and alcohol enhance its activity.
A nucleotide of adenine and one phosphate, the breakdown product of cAMP and a building block of RNA.
A second messenger formed from PIP2 by phospholipase C. It binds receptors on the endoplasmic reticulum to release calcium.
A gene for a receptor tyrosine kinase. Rearrangements occur in papillary thyroid cancer and activating mutations cause multiple endocrine neoplasia types 2A and 2B and medullary thyroid cancer.
The blood group system defined by A and B carbohydrate antigens on red cells. Type O people have anti-A and anti-B antibodies, so mismatched transfusion causes hemolysis.
A drug that blocks L-type calcium channels. Dihydropyridines (amlodipine) relax arteries; non-dihydropyridines (verapamil, diltiazem) also slow the heart.
The volume of plasma reaching the kidneys per minute, estimated by clearance of para-aminohippuric acid.
A stem cell disorder with PIGA mutation, so red cells lack GPI-anchored complement inhibitors (CD55, CD59). It causes complement-mediated hemolysis, dark urine and thrombosis.
The synapse between a motor neuron and skeletal muscle fiber, where acetylcholine acts on nicotinic receptors. Myasthenia gravis affects it.
The most common primary liver cancer, arising in cirrhosis or chronic hepatitis B or C. It secretes alpha-fetoprotein.
A nucleotide used to carry sugars, such as UDP-glucuronate in conjugation of bilirubin and drugs by glucuronyl transferase.
A membrane protein carrying glucose into cells by facilitated diffusion. GLUT4 is insulin-sensitive in muscle and fat; GLUT2 is in liver and beta cells.
A gene encoding a serine-threonine kinase in the MAPK pathway. The V600E mutation occurs in melanoma, papillary thyroid cancer and hairy cell leukemia, and is targeted by vemurafenib.
Infections spread by sexual contact, such as chlamydia, gonorrhea, syphilis, HPV and HIV.
An examination in which a gloved finger is inserted into the rectum to feel the prostate, sphincter tone and masses.

An inherited heart disease from sarcomere gene mutations causing asymmetric septal thickening that obstructs outflow. It presents with a systolic murmur increased by Valsalva and risk of sudden death.
Autoantibodies against neutrophil proteins, found in small-vessel vasculitides. c-ANCA (PR3) occurs in granulomatosis with polyangiitis; p-ANCA (MPO) in microscopic polyangiitis.
A platelet ADP receptor that promotes aggregation. Clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor block it.
An enveloped RNA paramyxovirus that causes bronchiolitis in infants. Palivizumab prevents it in high-risk infants.
A chloride channel gene on chromosome 7. Mutations (most often deltaF508) cause cystic fibrosis, with thick secretions, lung disease and pancreatic insufficiency.
A sensitive test that amplifies pathogen DNA or RNA, used to diagnose chlamydia, gonorrhea and many viral infections.
A neuron that runs from the brainstem or spinal cord to muscle. Lesions cause weakness with decreased tone, atrophy, fasciculations and absent reflexes.
A chronic inflammation and fibrosis of bile ducts causing beaded appearance on cholangiography. It is associated with ulcerative colitis and p-ANCA.
A condition after a traumatic event, with intrusive memories, avoidance, negative mood and hyperarousal lasting over 1 month.
Nothing by mouth: no food or drink, as when a patient has a bowel obstruction or is awaiting surgery.
An inhaled bronchodilator (salmeterol, formoterol) with 12-hour action, used with inhaled steroids in asthma and COPD maintenance.

term: Diphtheria, tetanus and acellular pertussis vaccine
def: A childhood vaccine containing diphtheria and tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis components.
A mild cervical dysplasia caused by HPV, often regressing spontaneously.
The endoplasmic reticulum studded with ribosomes, where secretory and membrane proteins are made and folded.
Malignant proliferation of breast duct epithelium confined by the basement membrane, often detected as calcifications on mammography.
The active form of folate, carrying one-carbon units for synthesis of purines and thymidylate.
A medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis with aneurysms causing a beaded appearance on angiography. It is associated with hepatitis B and spares the lungs.
A neutrophil enzyme that makes hypochlorous acid in the respiratory burst. Antibodies to it (p-ANCA) occur in microscopic polyangiitis.
Breathing tests (spirometry, lung volumes, diffusing capacity) that assess obstructive or restrictive lung disease.
Triglyceride-rich particles made by the liver that deliver fat to tissues. As lipoprotein lipase strips them, they become IDL and then LDL.
The percentage of hemoglobin binding oxygen in arterial blood. In methemoglobinemia, the measured pulse oximetry value stays near 85%.
The main adult hemoglobin, made of two alpha and two beta chains (alpha2beta2).
A standardized measure of prothrombin time used to monitor warfarin therapy.
Ventilatory support that keeps the airway open with constant pressure, used for obstructive sleep apnea.
The amino acid formed from tyrosine by tyrosine hydroxylase, which dopa decarboxylase converts to dopamine. Its levodopa form treats Parkinson disease.
A tumor marker elevated in colorectal and other cancers, used to monitor recurrence.
Enterococcus that carries vanA or vanB changing D-Ala-D-Ala to D-Ala-D-Lac, so vancomycin cannot bind. Treated with linezolid or daptomycin.
A neuropeptide that relaxes smooth muscle and stimulates intestinal secretion. A VIPoma causes watery diarrhea.
A POMC-derived hormone that stimulates melanocytes to produce pigment.
Nuclear receptors regulating fat and glucose metabolism. PPAR-gamma is the target of thiazolidinediones; PPAR-alpha is the target of fibrates.
A sodium channel in the collecting duct stimulated by aldosterone, blocked by amiloride and triamterene.
An autosomal dominant disorder from NF1 mutations with cafe-au-lait spots, neurofibromas, Lisch nodules and pheochromocytoma risk.
Small contraceptive devices placed in the uterus, either copper or progestin-releasing.
A cancer staging system based on primary tumor size (T), lymph node involvement (N) and metastasis (M).
An inflammatory bowel disease of the colon, starting in the rectum and extending continuously. It causes bloody diarrhea and has risk of colon cancer.
A kinase cascade (including Ras and Raf) that relays growth signals to the nucleus; dysregulation drives many cancers.
A recessive disorder of phenylalanine hydroxylase or tetrahydrobiopterin deficiency, so phenylalanine builds up. It causes intellectual disability and musty odor unless diet is controlled.
Recurrent upper airway collapse during sleep, causing snoring, daytime sleepiness and hypertension; treated with CPAP.
The coronary artery supplying the right atrium and ventricle and usually the inferior left ventricle, SA and AV nodes.
The height of the jugular vein pulsation, reflecting right atrial pressure. Raised in heart failure and tamponade.
A minor adult hemoglobin made of two alpha and two delta chains. It is elevated in beta-thalassemia.
A glycolysis intermediate in red cells that binds deoxyhemoglobin and lowers oxygen affinity. Fetal hemoglobin binds it poorly.
A glutamate-gated calcium channel involved in learning and excitotoxicity. Ketamine and dextromethorphan block it.
Inherited disease with many fluid-filled kidney cysts. The autosomal dominant form presents in adults; the recessive form in infants, with Potter sequence.
A lipoprotein formed as VLDL loses triglycerides, which then becomes LDL.
Nutrition given directly into a vein, bypassing the gut. Complications include cholestasis and line infection.
A mood disorder with depressed mood or anhedonia for at least 2 weeks plus other symptoms, such as sleep and appetite changes.
The probability that a person with a negative test truly lacks the disease. It falls as prevalence rises.
Venereal Disease Research Laboratory test, a nontreponemal syphilis screen detecting antibodies to cardiolipin. It can be falsely positive in lupus and antiphospholipid syndrome.
Surgery in which vein or artery grafts are used to bypass blocked coronary arteries.
HIV drugs (efavirenz, nevirapine) that bind a site on reverse transcriptase directly and block its activity.
A weak adrenal androgen made in the zona reticularis, converted to testosterone and estrogen in tissues.
A protein from osteoblasts that binds RANK on osteoclast precursors, stimulating bone resorption. Denosumab blocks it.
Treatment with estrogen with or without progestin to relieve menopausal symptoms, or replacement of other deficient hormones.
Autosomal dominant disease from VHL gene loss, causing hemangioblastomas, retinal angiomas, renal cell carcinoma and pheochromocytoma.
A transporter that moves glucose with sodium. SGLT2 in the proximal tubule reabsorbs filtered glucose and is blocked by gliflozin drugs.
A severe form of preeclampsia with Hemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes and Low Platelets.
A laboratory test that detects an antigen or antibody using an enzyme-linked antibody producing a color change, as in HIV screening.
A branch of the left main coronary artery supplying the lateral and posterior left ventricle.
Opening a blocked coronary artery with a catheter, balloon and stent. It is the preferred treatment for STEMI.
The resistance to flow in the lung circulation, calculated as mean pulmonary artery pressure minus wedge pressure divided by cardiac output.
A prostanoid (PGI2) made by endothelium that inhibits platelet aggregation and dilates vessels.
An immune reaction to heparin-platelet factor 4 complexes causing low platelets and paradoxical thrombosis, typically 5-10 days after starting heparin.
The volume of blood perfusing the kidneys per minute, about 20% of cardiac output.
An inherited disease from PKD1 or PKD2 mutation, causing bilateral renal cysts, hypertension and berry aneurysms, with progression to kidney failure.
Inflammation of the kidney interstitium, usually from drugs (penicillins, NSAIDs, PPIs), causing fever, rash and white blood cell casts.
A purine salvage enzyme. Its deficiency causes Lesch-Nyhan syndrome.
The average size of red cells, used to classify anemia as microcytic, normocytic or macrocytic.
A brainstem tract linking the cranial nerve nuclei for eye movement. A lesion causes internuclear ophthalmoplegia, as in multiple sclerosis.
A live attenuated Mycobacterium bovis vaccine against tuberculosis, also used for bladder cancer.
A knee ligament that prevents forward tibial displacement. Tears produce anterior drawer and Lachman signs.
A skin or specimen scraping treated with KOH to dissolve host cells and show fungal hyphae under a microscope.
Abnormal hip joint formation in which the femoral head is unstable or dislocated. Screened by Ortolani and Barlow maneuvers.
Monitoring of fetal heart rate with movement. A reactive test shows accelerations; a nonreactive one needs more testing.
A Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (O157:H7) causing bloody diarrhea and hemolytic uremic syndrome, from undercooked beef.
A family of liver enzymes that metabolize drugs and steroids. Inducers or inhibitors cause many drug interactions.
The most severe lupus nephritis (class IV), with subendothelial immune complexes and wire-loop lesions.
A ribose phosphate donor for purine and pyrimidine synthesis. It activates carbamoyl phosphate synthetase II.
Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms: fever, rash, eosinophilia and organ involvement weeks after starting a drug such as allopurinol or anticonvulsants.
A tyrosine kinase in cytokine signaling. The V617F mutation occurs in polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia and myelofibrosis.
An autosomal dominant syndrome from APC mutation with hundreds of colon polyps and near-certain colon cancer if the colon is not removed.
The knuckle joint between metacarpal and finger bone; involved in rheumatoid arthritis and hemochromatosis.
An autoimmune disease against presynaptic calcium channels, causing proximal weakness that improves with use, linked to small cell lung cancer.
Short-wavelength UV (280-315 nm) that causes sunburn and DNA pyrimidine dimers; narrowband UVB is used to treat psoriasis.
A daily hormone pill (estrogen and progestin or progestin only) that prevents ovulation.
A chemokine receptor on T cells and macrophages that HIV uses as a co-receptor. Maraviroc blocks it.
Rapid destruction of transfused red cells by preformed antibodies in ABO mismatch (type II hypersensitivity), causing fever, hypotension and hemoglobinuria.
Cardiovascular disease caused by atherosclerosis, including coronary disease, stroke and peripheral artery disease.
A 3-15 score of eye opening, verbal and motor response to assess consciousness.
A precursor cleaved into ACTH, MSH and beta-endorphin.
An autoantibody that activates the TSH receptor in Graves disease, causing hyperthyroidism.
Fatty acids released from triglycerides into the blood, bound to albumin, for use as fuel.
The most common adult kidney cancer, from proximal tubule cells. It presents with hematuria, flank mass and polycythemia; smoking and VHL are risks.
A technique using fluorescent DNA probes to detect specific chromosomal sequences or translocations.
A heart attack with myocardial necrosis (rising troponin) but no ST elevation on ECG.
Cardiac ultrasound through the chest wall to assess valves, chambers and function.
A brief episode of focal neurologic deficit from temporary ischemia without infarction, resolving within 24 hours.
A riboflavin-derived coenzyme in redox reactions such as succinate dehydrogenase and the citric acid cycle.
A cause of nephrotic syndrome with scarring of parts of some glomeruli. It is common in Black adults, HIV and heroin use.
A liver enzyme raised in cholestasis and alcohol use. It helps confirm that elevated alkaline phosphatase is from liver.
An early heartbeat from the ventricles with wide QRS and no P wave; often benign.
A folate antagonist that inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking thymidylate and purine synthesis. Used for cancers and autoimmune disease; toxicities include myelosuppression and hepatotoxicity.
Neurons running from the brainstem or spinal cord to muscle, damage to which causes flaccid weakness, atrophy and fasciculations.
MRI imaging of the bile and pancreatic ducts without contrast or endoscopy.
